claim: The Epic Games Store on mobile (Android + iOS, aggregated across all launched countries including the EU) reached only 29 million installs by January 2025, missing Epic's own stated target of 100 million installs by end of 2024 by 71 million.
stance_target: alternative iOS marketplace adoption has been slow/small relative to operator expectations, bounding the speed of App Store commission erosion
scope_conditions: global, Android + iOS combined, August 2024 launch through January 2025; NOT an EU-only or iOS-only figure
quoted_support: There have been 29 million installs of the Epic Games Store on mobile devices since we launched, well short of our goal of 100 million installs by the end of 2024.

claim: More than 50% of user attempts to install the Epic Games Store on Android or iOS fail, which Epic attributes to Apple's and Google's multi-step warning ('scare screen') install flows.
stance_target: friction in Apple's install flow materially suppresses realized alternative-marketplace adoption versus intent
scope_conditions: Epic's own self-reported install funnel data, as of January 2025
quoted_support: So far, more than 50% of the time a player tries to install the Epic Games Store on Android or iOS they are unsuccessful due to onerous scare screens.

claim: In the EU specifically, an additional 5 million attempts to install the Epic Games Store were blocked by Apple's browser and operating-system 'Eligibility Requirements' checks, per Epic's own disclosure.
stance_target: Apple retains technical gatekeeping mechanisms in the EU that suppress alternative-marketplace installs even post-DMA
scope_conditions: European Union specifically, as of January 2025, self-reported by Epic (a litigant against Apple)
quoted_support: In the European Union, an additional 5 million attempts to install the Epic Games Store were blocked by Apple's browser and operating system 'Eligibility Requirements'.
numbers: 5 million blocked install attempts in the EU

claim: As of January 2025, none of the 100 highest-grossing mobile game developers were willing to distribute their games on the Epic Games Store because of Apple's Core Technology Fee and associated restrictions.
stance_target: supply-side (developer) adoption of alternative marketplaces has also been minimal, not just demand-side
scope_conditions: top 100 highest-grossing mobile game developers globally, as of January 2025
quoted_support: So far none of the 100 highest grossing mobile game developers are willing to distribute their games on the Epic Games Store because of the Core Technology Fee and Apple and Google's onerous restrictions and scare screens.
numbers: EUR0.50 Core Technology Fee per install above 1M/year threshold

claim: Setapp Mobile, a EUR9.99/month subscription alternative iOS marketplace launched September 2024, shut down in February 2026 after roughly 17 months, with MacPaw stating the business was not commercially viable under Apple's fee structure.
stance_target: commercial non-viability, not just slow adoption, bounds how large alternative-marketplace-driven commission erosion can become in the near term
scope_conditions: single marketplace operator (MacPaw/Setapp Mobile), EU, September 2024-February 2026
quoted_support: As a result of still-evolving commercial conditions, we have determined that it is not viable to continue development or support for Setapp Mobile within Setapp's current business model.

claim: No official European Commission compliance-monitoring report, court filing, or third-party analytics firm (Sensor Tower, Appfigures, Analysis Group) publishes a measured percentage of EU iPhone users who have downloaded or actively use an alternative iOS app marketplace, as of the search date.
stance_target: existence of an authoritative EU alternative-marketplace adoption-rate figure
scope_conditions: web-searchable English-language sources as of September 2026 fetch date; official EC DMA decisions (19 Mar 2025 specification decisions, 23 Apr 2025 non-compliance decision/EUR500m fine) and analyst commentary reviewed
quoted_support: the search results do not include specific statistics about what percentage of iPhone users in the EU have adopted alternative app marketplaces
